body:
### Problem

When viewing a file in nvim (e.g. `some_dir/some_file.txt`) and then deleting that file's parent directory via another process (e.g. `git rm -r some_dir`), nvim becomes unresponsive, repeatedly showing the following in the message area:

```lua
Lua callback:
C:/Program Files/Neovim/share/nvim/runtime/lua/vim/log.lua:107: attempt to index local 'info' (a nil value)
stack traceback:
        C:/Program Files/Neovim/share/nvim/runtime/lua/vim/log.lua:107: in function 'format_func'
        C:/Program Files/Neovim/share/nvim/runtime/lua/vim/log.lua:236: in function <C:/Program Files/Neovim/share/nvim/runtime/lua/vim/log.lua:228>
```

This was using NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1583+gd039f19af5.  Using a prior build (v0.13.0-dev-1572+g318ea4de21), the result was the same but the error was in ..share/nvim/runtime/lua/vim/_watch.lua and contained `EPERM` (sorry, didn't save the error /call stack).

If only the file is removed, but not it's parent directory, nvim displays the more familiar `E211: File "some_dir/somefile.txt" no longer available` and is still responsive.

Might be related to issue #32386? And I believe the error changed (from somewhere in `_watch.lua` to `log.lua`)  when pr #41776 was merged.

P.S. If you enable `:h ui2`, you don't have to kill the nvim process; you are able to exit normally.




### Steps to reproduce

1. create a directory, create a file in that directory (e.g. `~/some_dir` and `~/some_dir/some_file.txt`)
2. open the file in nvim (`nvim --clean .\some_dir\some_file.txt`)
3. in another terminal pane delete the directory (`rm -r .\some_dir`)


### Expected behavior

nvim displays the same message as when just the file (not it's whole parent directory) is removed by another process: `E211: File "some_dir/somefile.txt" no longer available`



### Nvim version (nvim -v)

v0.13.0-dev-1583+gd039f19af5

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

na

### Operating system/version

Windows 11

### Terminal name/version

Windows Terminal Preview / 1.25.1912.0

### $TERM environment variable

na

### Installation

download nvim-win64.zip from releases
title: nvim becomes unresponsive when another process deletes the parent directory of a file that nvim has an open buffer to (on Windows)
